summary:
The headline this week is the phillipsben site assistant going fully live. Six phases, start to finish: a build-time knowledge pack (~12k tokens of site content, with a redaction guard that makes confidential leaks structurally impossible), a `/ask` API route with pluggable LLM backend and per-IP rate limiting, a streaming chat overlay with focus-trap and mobile layout, a loud hero band with chip shortcuts, and adversarial hardening. The battery ran 16/16 with zero leaks — fabrication, off-topic, prompt-injection, and open-relay attempts all handled cleanly. The flagship write-up at `/projects/site-assistant/` shipped last, so the bot can answer questions about itself.

The backend decision was a deliberate engineering call: the local Tesla P100 option exists and is wired (via Switchboard), but warm prefill latency on the P100 sits around 10s with full context, cold around 48s. Claude Haiku was chosen as the default for responsiveness, with the local path kept as an opt-in.

On the homelab side, Switchboard (the FastAPI proxy that serializes GPU access across KoboldCPP, ComfyUI, and Ollama) got its site-assistant endpoint wired in the same push — priority-aware lock, bearer auth, warm fast-path, and a `429 preempt_timeout` safety valve so the site falls back to Haiku instead of hanging. A side investigation into routing Gemma 4 (26B MoE) through llama.cpp for expert offloading was scoped and deferred — it needs a custom CUDA container for sm_60 and a new eviction strategy in the broker.

highlights.oneLiner: Site assistant shipped end-to-end — knowledge pack, chat overlay, hero band, adversarial hardening (16/16), and flagship write-up all live on main.
Daily dashboard cron stable; pop-os memory snapshot syncing fresh each morning.
